A periodic table for THE LETTERS LEDGER. Every possibility shown here is unconfirmed. The ternary arithmetic, the codes, the card names, the knot: settled, keeper-independent, pinned by test. The letters beneath them: not sealed to any public reading surface, held open at the keeper's gate.
THE MAP ROOM THE LETTERS LEDGER

Laid out like a table of elements: the knot crowns each cell, the seat number in its corner, and beneath the knot the letter sits between two fixed companions — the ternary code stacked dot · bar · wave (field down to core, the canon's own three marks) on one side, and on the other a family symbol, the same rotational count as the knot above it (one ring, a vesica, a trefoil, a sevenfold rosette) distilled to its plainest form. Only the badge at centre changes hands. The canon commits every shape here letter-free by construction, before any letter ever touches them — so a resemblance you read into one is your own eye, the same register as “SH sounds like S,” not a second, independent proof. Worth looking at for exactly that reason: not instead of the keeper's own hand, alongside it.
